name: TDengine
tagline: Industrial-IoT time-series database with a table-per-device model and built-in streaming and caching.
description: TDengine, from TAOS Data, is a distributed time-series database designed around industrial IoT. Each device gets its own sub-table under a shared "super table" schema, which keeps writes sequential and per-device queries fast, while tags on the super table drive fleet-wide aggregation. It bundles features other stacks bolt on, including stream processing, Kafka-style data subscription, last-value caching and retention, so one cluster can stand in for a broker, a TSDB and a cache for sensor data. The open-source edition is AGPL-3.0 and includes clustering; TDengine Enterprise and TDengine Cloud add tiered storage, backup and connectors to industrial sources such as OPC and PI.

pricing.notes: Open-source edition is free; Enterprise is a subscription; TDengine Cloud is usage-based.

scale.notes: Data is split into virtual nodes (vnodes) replicated with Raft and spread across dnodes.

strengths: Super-table model fits fleets of millions of devices sharing a schema
Built-in stream processing, data subscription and last-value cache reduce extra infrastructure
Columnar per-device storage gives high compression on sensor data
Accepts InfluxDB line protocol and OpenTSDB writes in schemaless mode
Clustering is included in the open-source edition
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 licence is a hurdle for embedding in commercial products
SQL dialect has restrictions (joins mainly on timestamps, limited updates)
Community and docs are strongest in China; English ecosystem is smaller
Table-per-device design suits regular telemetry better than ad-hoc event data
useCases: Industrial IoT and SCADA historian replacement
notIdealFor: Irregular event data without a stable schema
